gates.checked: The address this application is actually serving on.
The Node major version, platform and architecture this process is executing on.
The scheme this application serves on, and whether it can be reached from off the host.
gates.observed: Serving HTTP on loopback, so no request crosses a network.

gates.checked: Whether the database is configured to survive a power loss.
Whether an active primary owner exists in the local identity store.
Whether the public key identifiers needed to verify trusted input are configured.

Whether a backup snapshot has been declared for this installation and whether a restore from one has been reconciled against current consent and released from quarantine. This product does not make, hold or read the archive, so it is not evidence that the archive exists or can be read -- only that a snapshot was declared and a restore was carried through.
gates.observed: No snapshot has ever been declared. No restore has been reconciled and released.
gates.remedy: Declare a snapshot when the archive is taken, and carry a restore through quarantine and reconciliation at least once. An untested restore is the failure this gate exists to catch, and this product cannot see the archive itself: reading it back is still a job for the customer’s own tooling.

gates.checked: That no guided connection records an endpoint outside loopback, and that this build declares no vendor egress.
The telemetry switches of every third-party component, read from the running environment.
Whether a signed licence is within its validity window.
Whether the installed version has a signed release manifest verified at import.
gates.remedy: Record the installed version through the update path so the package behind it can be named and its signature checked.

limits: A gate this build cannot check reports that it could not, with the reason, and is not counted as passed.
These are eleven technical checks against this installation. Passing them is not a statement that any legal obligation has been met.
